Q: Heatmap in Grafana A:

I don't think that's really possible with the heatmap visualization given your input data. If you had the raw (non-aggregated) data, it's possible. Grafana requires a timeseries with bucket bounds as dimension (see Introduction to histograms and heatmaps.

The closest I could get was with a XY Chart (a.k.a. scatter plot), mapping your date column to X, your "Amount bin" to Y, and "# of transactions" to the size. That would give you something like this:

Q: Trying to write a code that gets an array of random temperature readings for 14 days. Then outputs the high/low temps and averages on those days A:

The printGreeting proc is ok, but to me it seems a bit convoluted with these three arguments. One argument to a single cartouche would be much cleaner.

Now the real problems start early in the program!

  • For generating the temperatures you invoke generateTemperatures with a single argument, yet you return from it using ret 8. Your stack is already corrupted! (Also what about the incomplete procedure header?)
  • The findDailyHighs and findDailyLows procs are very similar, and indeed you copy-pasted here and left some redundant instructions while doing so! Several things got wrong:
    • You got source and destination reversed. The offset to the temperature array was pushed last, so that resides at `[ebp+8] and must go to ESI.
    • The inner loop is set to perform one iteration too many. With 11 items there can be but 10 comparisons.
    • The inner loop can not be using the loop instruction. It is meant to use EBX instead (dec ebx jnz _inner)
  • The displayTempArray and displayTempWithStrings procs got lots of arguments (8 and 4) but both return through a naked ret. This leaves the arguments on the stack!
  • It's been a long time I looked at irvine's but does writeInt really expect EDX for its argument? Shouldn't it be EAX?
  • The name displayTempArray clearly suggests processing the full array, yet you haven't written a loop that iterates over the array's elements. A work in progress no doubt?

Finally there's the orphan proc calAverageLowHighTemps. It is called from nowhere, and for now that is a good thing as it contains the dreaded division exception in the (twice repeated) instruction pair loop _cal... div ecx. Remember ECX=0 after loop completion.

You need to take this one step at a time. You got way to much untested code already!
A first step should be to successfully

  • print your opening cartouche
  • generate the temperature array
  • print the temperature array

Once this truly works, you add one extra piece of code an run it again. Don't add more until it works fine. Good luck!

One additional error that I forgot to mention:

; findDailyLows
PUSH OFFSET low_daily
PUSH temp_array
CALL findDailyLows

See how you omitted the OFFSET specifier here?
The proc is expecting an address, but push temp_array just passes the value of the first element of the array.

Q: Architectural differences between Laravel + Inertia (Vue) and Laravel API + React SPA A:

Inertia has a React adapter so I think it comes down to Vue vs React which (in my opinion) is really personal preference.

There are probably tons of articles comparing the two. I think that under the hood they work very similarly and can do similar things (Vue even can be configured to define components using JSX) so overall I'd pick what I'm most familiar with (or what is most widely used in the broader area of where I work). Ecosystem-wise I do think React is a winner because it is more widely adopted and is backed by a major corporation but you may not need this wider support for your particular use case and all the basics are covered in both.
